live.name: BRONZE SATIN
live.headline: BRONZE SATIN: what the catalogue records about this tracked threat actor
live.in_short: BRONZE SATIN is Secureworks' name for an actor also tracked as HAFNIUM, Murky Panda and Silk Typhoon. The catalogue lists two web shell tools. No report card gives more detail.

sentences.t: BRONZE SATIN is the name used in the Secureworks entry for this threat actor.
The catalogue lists three other names for the same actor: HAFNIUM, Murky Panda and Silk Typhoon.
The catalogue lists two tools for this actor: ChinaChopper and Godzilla Webshell.

next.in_short: BRONZE SATIN is Secureworks' name for an actor also tracked as HAFNIUM, Murky Panda and Silk Typhoon. The UK assesses it was highly likely behind the 2021 Exchange server intrusions.

sentences.t: Secureworks tracks this actor as BRONZE SATIN.
Other names for the same actor are HAFNIUM, Murky Panda and Silk Typhoon.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre says HAFNIUM is associated with the Chinese state.
Italian media (ANSA), as relayed by BleepingComputer, describe Silk Typhoon, also called Hafnium, as a Chinese state-sponsored group.

BleepingComputer reports that Italian media tie Silk Typhoon to 2020 attacks on infectious disease researchers and healthcare organisations. The aim was said to be data on anti-COVID vaccines. The report does not confirm these ties.
The same report says the group has targeted American organisations and government agencies.
The catalogue lists two tools for this actor: ChinaChopper and Godzilla Webshell.
BleepingComputer says Microsoft reported in March that Silk Typhoon had begun targeting remote management tools and cloud services.
A blogger's educational post on dumping Windows credential memory says HAFNIUM and Fox Kitten used a related dumping tool.
In July 2021 the UK's NCSC assessed it was highly likely that HAFNIUM was responsible for early-2021 intrusions through Microsoft Exchange servers.
The UK statement cites open-source reporting that at least 30,000 organisations were compromised in the US alone.
The NCSC says it issued tailored advice to over 70 affected organisations.
On 3 July 2025, Italian police arrested a 33-year-old man, Xu Zewei, at Milan's Malpensa Airport on a U.S. warrant. Italian media (ANSA) allege he is linked to Silk Typhoon.
The U.S. is seeking his extradition for trial. The report does not give an extradition decision.
Keep internet-facing servers and remote management tools patched, and watch them for web shells and unusual credential access.
